Intro

Strattera (atomoxetine) is a medication used for treatment of ADHD, it works by selectively inhibiting the reuptake of norepinephrine in the frontal lobe of the brain

Strattera is generally well tolerated by most patients, but it sometimes may lead to side effects that will be mentioned here

Every person will have a different experience with side effects

By VisualBeo, CC3.0, via Wikimedia commons

1. Increased heart rate and blood pressure

Strattera inhibit norepinephrine reuptake leading to higher levels of norepinephrine

This will lead to sympathetic nervous system activation => activation of adrenergic receptors in the heart and blood vessels leading to elevated heart rate and blood pressure

If patients stop the medication then it is probably due to this side effects

YitzhakNat, CC BY-SA 4.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0>, via Wikimedia Commons

2. Mood Swings and Insomnia

Higher levels of norepinephrine in certain brain regions lead to mood swings and insomnia

https://www.myupchar.com/en, CC BY-SA 4.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0>, via Wikimedia Commons

3. GIT side effects

Nausea, vomiting and decreased appetite

That is because Increased norepinephrine levels also affects the enteric nervous system leading to nausea, vomiting and decreased appetite

Also Elevated norepinephrine levels may stimulate the chemoreceptor trigger zone in the brain leading to nausea and vomiting

4. Hepatotoxicity

Strattera is metabolized in the liver and in rare cases it may cause damage to the liver

There might be an immune mediated component of the Strattera hepatotoxicity

Symptoms include yellow, skin and eye, itching, upper abdominal pain and dark urine

Laboratoires Servier, CC BY-SA 3.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0>, via Wikimedia Commons

5. Urinary symptoms

Difficulty urinating and rarely urinary retention

Norepinephrine affects alpha adrenergic receptors in the urinary tract which lead to contraction of the bladder sphincter muscles causing difficulty in urination and urinary retention

7. Sexual side effects

Decreased libido in males and females, weak erections and difficulty ejaculating in males

Norepinephrine can affect the alpha adrenergic receptors in the genital region, which can affect blood flow and nerve signaling leading to sexual side effects

8. Allergic reactions

Ranges from mild rashes to severe angioedema

9. Weight loss

Higher levels of norepinephrine may suppress the appetite centers in the hypothalamus leading to anorexia and weight loss
